comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Implementation progress + one design decision that needed deciding before AC2.

AC1 + AC3 are implemented in worktree `impl-cb1b` (ruff check/format clean, module imports):

- `_code_review_variant(base, head, source)` — code review is RANGE-scoped, not ticket-scoped,
  so the dedup variant carries `base`/`head`. `begin_gate_job` receives an empty `ticket_id`;
  `canonical_ticket_id` is documented best-effort and returns its input unchanged on any
  resolution failure, so an empty id passes through safely rather than raising.
- `_review_code_body(base, head, ref, source)` — extracted from the `review_code` tool so the
  sync tool and the starter structure an LLM failure identically. Without the shared body a
  starter would RAISE where the sync tool RETURNS a structured dict, settling the daemon as
  `failed` for a condition the sync path reports as an ordinary result.
- `review_code_start` — mirrors `review_plan_start`, including the
  `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` offload (basis resolution and index writes block the event loop).
- AC3: `_gate_sidecar_fields`'s hard-coded `{"plan_review","verify_completion"}` is replaced by
  module constant `GATE_TYPES_WITH_SIDECARS`, now including `code_review`, so `gate_status` no
  longer silently drops its replay provenance.

DESIGN DECISION for AC2 — the async claim/close starters must NOT reuse the gate's own
`gate_type`.

`transition_ticket` and `claim_ticket` are declarative `ToolSpec`s (`_mcp_tool_specs.py:649`),
dispatched to `rebar.<library>`; they have no hand-written body to make async. Their starters
therefore need the bespoke daemon path, not a spec.

The trap: a claim RUNS the plan-review gate and a gated close RUNS completion verification. If
their starters key on `gate_type="plan_review"` / `"verify_completion"`, then
`compute_key(gate_type, ticket, basis, variant, readonly)` makes a `claim_ticket_start` collide
with an already-running `review_plan_start` for the same ticket and basis. The claim would
ATTACH to the review-only job, report `passed`, and never perform the transition — a silent
no-op close. So the starters take distinct gate types (`claim` / `transition`); the gate still
runs inside the work unit, but job identity stays separate.

Housing: `_mcp_tool_specs.py` is 738 LOC against the 800 cap (62 lines headroom), so the
starters cannot go there. `_mcp_llm.py` is 507 after the AC1/AC3 edits. Leaning toward a
separate module for the ticket-op starters consuming `_start_gate_job`, rather than growing
`_mcp_llm.py` with ops that are not LLM tools.

Remaining: AC2 (claim/transition starters), AC4 (test that the handle returns BEFORE the gate
completes — a terminal-verdict-only test does not cover the bug), AC5 (invariant guard: every
gate-running MCP tool has an async counterpart), AC6 (docs + the AGENTS.md guidance that
currently names only `review_plan`/`verify_completion`), AC7 (dedup seam).

comments.body:
All 7 ACs implemented in worktree `impl-cb1b`. `make verify` running; nothing pushed yet.

**AC4 — the handle returns BEFORE the gate completes.** Parametrized over all three new
starters (`review_code_start`, `claim_ticket_start`, `transition_ticket_start`). The blocked
library op (`rebar.llm.review_code` / `rebar.claim` / `rebar.transition`) holds a
`threading.Event` for the whole scenario, so a start body that blocked on the gate could
never return; `anyio.fail_after(3)` makes that a deterministic failure instead of a hang,
and `elapsed < 2` plus a mid-run `gate_status(...) == "running"` assertion pins the
immediate return. A terminal-verdict-only test would pass against the blocking code that
caused this bug, which is why the AC called that out.

**AC5 — the invariant guard is non-vacuous.** Measured against the REAL `build_server()`,
not a hand-built subset: 67 tools, and all 5 of `review_plan` / `verify_completion` /
`review_code` / `claim_ticket` / `transition_ticket` now have both a base tool and a
`*_start`. Before this change only 2 did, so the guard would have failed on 3. A second test
keeps the hand-maintained roster honest by cross-checking the billable LLM gate tools
against it; `scan_spec` is excluded with a stated reason (billable, but not one of the three
gates, so cb1b's invariant does not reach it).

**AC7 — dedup.** Parametrized per starter: a second start fired while the first is provably
still blocked inside the op returns the SAME `job_id`, and the op ran exactly once. That is
the re-fire reflex this bug provokes, so it is the case that must not double-bill.

**Collision test for the AC2 decision.** `claim_ticket_start` fired against a live
`review_plan_start` for the same ticket gets a different `job_id` AND a different
`gate_type`, and the claim really runs rather than inheriting the review's `passed`. Without
the distinct `claim`/`transition` gate types this is a silent no-op claim — worse than the
timeout being fixed.

**AC6 — `docs/mcp-reference.md` is GENERATED, with a CI drift gate.** Hand-editing it would
have been reverted by the next regeneration. The real defect was upstream:
`scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` enumerates registrars explicitly and knew only 3, so the new
`register_ticket_async_tools` was invisible to it — the generated doc said 65 tools while
the server had 67. Folded the new registrar into the write-gated group (its starters are
write-gated mutations, so they belong beside the `claim_ticket`/`transition_ticket` they
front). Regenerated: 64 -> 67. `AGENTS.md`'s async-gate bullet, which named only
`review_plan`/`verify_completion`, now names all five starters, states that a gated claim
and a completion-verified close BOTH time out over MCP, and records that the ticket
starters apply their status change only when the gate passes.

**Tests:** `tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py` 37 passed. Targeted sweep
`-k "mcp or surface or docs or parity"`: 1018 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed — including the
generated-artifact drift gates that the doc regeneration had to satisfy.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

`transition_ticket(fattish-plucky-bufflehead, "in_progress" -> "closed")` over MCP
returned `McpError: -32001: Request timed out` on three successive attempts. The
ticket stayed `in_progress` each time. The call runs the completion-verifier close
gate inline, and that gate takes 9-11 minutes by `AGENTS.md`'s own published
estimate, against an MCP client request deadline of roughly 60 seconds.

The timeout is not a verdict. The server keeps running, the caller learns nothing,
and the natural response is to re-fire the same call -- a second billable gate pass.
This is precisely the failure `AGENTS.md` already describes for the direct gate
tools, and the reason `review_plan_start` / `verify_completion_start` exist.

## Why the existing workaround does not cover it

Pre-computing the attestation does NOT make the close fast. Measured on
`62dc-535b-5d05-421d` at `origin/main` `f1fe7c6f587d3a57fcd4b49598485d7fd4101711`:

1. `verify_completion_start` -> job
   `1793725995508270393-89be127e921a4bf8b7acd1bbfaee7749`.
2. `gate_status` -> `status: "passed"`, `verdict: "PASS"`,
   `verified_at_sha: f1fe7c6f587...`, `signed_at: 1793726842234944794`.
3. `transition_ticket` with that signed certificate in place -> **timed out again**.

So the async surface covers the gate op but not the operation that actually needs
it. An agent that follows the documented guidance still cannot close a ticket over
MCP without an ambiguous timeout.

## Scope: which surfaces run a gate with no async counterpart

In `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, `_start_gate_job` and `_spawn_gate_daemon` are already generic
over `gate_type` -- the daemon machinery is not the gap; only two gates use it:
- `_register_gate_start_tools` registers exactly two starters: `review_plan_start` and
  `verify_completion_start`.
- `rebar/llm/gate_runs.py` (`_durable_verdict`), the `gate_status` docstring in
  `_mcp_reads.py`, and `schemas/gate_run.schema.json` describe only those two job kinds.

Surfaces that run one of the long gates inline with NO async form:

| Surface | Gate run inline | Async form |
|---|---|---|
| `transition_ticket` (`_mcp_tool_specs.py`) | completion-verifier on a close (`transition_close.close_ticket`) | none |
| `review_code` (`_mcp_llm.py`) | four-pass code review | none |

Out of the gate-running scope, verified in code: `claim_ticket` and the `open -> in_progress`
branch of `transition_ticket` go through `gates.plan_review_precheck`, which only calls
`llm.claim_gate_check` -- a local HMAC + freshness check with no LLM and no network call
(`_commands/gates.py:319-366`). They return in milliseconds and need no starter. The
`claim --review` flag that does run `llm.review_plan` is CLI-only and not exposed over MCP.

`review_code` is the clearest gap: a long LLM gate op registered synchronously alongside
`review_plan` and `verify_completion`, which both got starters.

## Invariant to establish

Every MCP surface that runs the plan-review, completion-verifier, or code-review gate must
have an async counterpart returning a `{job_id, ..., status: "running"}` handle pollable by
`gate_status`, so no caller is ever forced into a request that can outlive the client
deadline. Today the invariant holds for 2 surfaces (`review_plan`, `verify_completion`) and
fails for 2 (`review_code`, `transition_ticket`).

## Design

- `review_code_start` (in `_mcp_llm.py`) mirrors `review_plan_start`, with gate type
  `code_review`, an empty `ticket_id` (a code review covers a git range), and a dedup variant
  carrying `base`/`head`/`source`. The sync `review_code` and the starter share one body
  (`_review_code_body`) so a provider failure is the same structured result on both, and the
  sync tool goes through `run_gate_singleflight` with the same key.
- `transition_ticket_start` (new `src/rebar/_mcp_ticket_async.py`) wraps the SAME derived
  `transition_ticket` tool (spec pre/post hooks included) and runs it on the gate daemon via
  `_start_gate_job`. It uses its own gate type `transition`, not `verify_completion`: the dedup
  key starts with the gate type, so reusing `verify_completion` would let a close ATTACH to a
  running `verify_completion_start`, report that check's `passed`, and never transition. A
  completed transition settles `passed` with verdict `applied`; a refusal (gate FAIL,
  ConcurrencyError) settles `failed` with the message in `error`. Registered from
  `mcp_server.build_server` and skipped on a read-only server, like the write tools.
- `_terminal_from_result` unwraps the nested code-review verdict dict (`review_result` carries
  the typed gate verdict under `verdict`) to its PASS/BLOCK string for the run index.
- `gate_runs._durable_verdict` maps a `transition` job to the ticket's completion-certificate
  currency, so a close poller sees whether the completion cert persisted.
- `_gate_sidecar_fields` is unchanged: no code-review path produces the `sidecar_emitted` /
  `sidecar_reviewed_at` fields it copies, so a `code_review` job has no sidecar provenance to
  keep.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 -- `review_code_start` exists, returns a `{job_id, ticket_id, gate_type,
  status: "running"}` handle in milliseconds, and its job is pollable through `gate_status` to
  a terminal `passed`/`failed` carrying the review's PASS/BLOCK verdict.
- [ ] AC2 -- `transition_ticket_start` starts the transition (and its completion-verifier close
  gate) on a daemon, returns a handle immediately, and applies the status change only on gate
  success -- so a close over MCP is never blocked on an inline gate run.
- [ ] AC3 -- `gate_status` reports the new `code_review` and `transition` job kinds (gate type,
  verdict, and for `transition` the durable completion currency). The `gate_status` docstring
  and the `GateRun` schema description name every starter.
- [ ] AC4 -- a test drives each new starter through `gate_status` to a terminal state,
  asserting the handle returned BEFORE the gate completed (a terminal-verdict-only test would
  pass against the blocking code this bug is about).
- [ ] AC5 -- a test asserts the invariant directly against the real `build_server()`: every
  registered MCP tool that runs one of the three gates has a `<name>_start` counterpart, and a
  second test classifies every billable LLM tool so a new gate surface cannot ship without one.
- [ ] AC6 -- `docs/mcp-reference.md` (regenerated by `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py`, which must
  enumerate the new registrar) documents the new starters, and the `AGENTS.md` async-gate
  guidance that names only `review_plan` / `verify_completion` is widened to every
  gate-running surface.
- [ ] AC7 -- de-dup protection applies to the new surfaces as it does to synchronous
  `review_plan` / `verify_completion`: a re-fire while a run is in flight attaches to it (same
  `job_id`, one gate run) instead of double-billing.

## Provider neutrality

Nothing here is provider- or model-specific. The daemon machinery, job handle, and polling
surface are all transport-level and indifferent to which provider backs a gate.

## Out of scope

- Changing any gate's verdict logic, prompt, or criteria.
- Raising the MCP client request deadline -- a client setting, and it would not fix a
  10-minute gate behind a 60-second deadline anyway.
- CLI surfaces, which are not subject to the MCP request deadline.
